meta.title: d3
meta.description: Decision 3.0's 27B decision model: answers typed questions (choice, yes / no, score) about text, JSON, images and videos with a probability for every option, without generating text.
meta.performance_headline: MI300X: 415 of 416 decisions match the checkpoint runtime (one near-tie); MI325X: 1.8x its server's requests per second at 64 clients

recommended_command.docker_command:
docker run --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --group-add video \
  --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly vllm-sr/d3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1

strategy_spec.name: single_node_tp
strategy_spec.description: Single-node tensor parallel. Splits the model across all local GPUs. TP size is set to the GPU count at deploy time. The simplest multi-GPU strategy — works for all model architectures.

default.description: BF16 weights (52.2 GB) and an FP32 answer-code readout

guide:
## Overview

[vllm-sr/d3](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3) is the 27B model of Decision 3.0, the decision models of
[vLLM Semantic Router](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router). Give it a state (text or JSON,
optionally with images and videos) and typed questions: pick one of several options (`choice`), yes or no
(`noul`), or a level on a scale (`score`). It returns a probability for every option, without generating text.

It is a backbone of the Qwen3.5 architecture (26.09B parameters, including the 0.46B vision
encoder), trained from `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, with an answer-code readout. vLLM detects the checkpoint's `decision_config.json` and serves it
as a classification model (`D3ForSequenceClassification`) on its System One endpoint, `/v1/systemone`: one
forward pass per question, whose readout scores that question's options at the last token. The full attention
layers read the prompt in both directions, so chunked prefill and prefix caching are off.

The Decision 3.0 models, all served the same way:

- [`vllm-sr/d3`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3) (27B) — this recipe
- [`vllm-sr/d3-flash`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-flash) (9B)
- [`vllm-sr/d3-mini`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-mini) (4B)
- [`vllm-sr/d3-nano`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-nano) (2B)
- [`vllm-sr/d3-lite`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-lite) (0.8B)
- [`vllm-sr/d3-edge`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-edge) (0.6B)

## Prerequisites

- **Hardware**: one GPU. The BF16 weights take 52.2 GB; vLLM reserves 92 % of the GPU's memory by default.
- **vLLM**: a nightly build. Decision 3.0 support ([vllm-project/vllm#61565](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61565))
  is on vLLM main since 2026-10-14 and not in a release yet (the latest, v0.31.0, does not include it).
  Every nightly built since 2026-10-15 includes it.
- **ROCm**: Python 3.12, glibc 2.39 or newer (for example Ubuntu 24.04), and the system libraries
  `libopenmpi3t64` and `libdw1t64`, which the ROCm wheels load at import.

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 --seed
source .venv/bin/activate

# NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA)
uv pip install -U vllm --torch-backend=auto --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly

# AMD GPUs (ROCm 7.2; glibc 2.39 or newer, as on Ubuntu 24.04)
sudo apt install -y libopenmpi3t64 libdw1t64
export VLLM_ROCM_VARIANT=$(curl -s https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/nightly | grep -oP 'rocm\d+' | head -1 | sed 's/%2B/+/g')
uv pip install --pre vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/nightly/${VLLM_ROCM_VARIANT} --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
```

## Launch

```bash
vllm serve vllm-sr/d3
```

No flags are needed; the first start downloads the model.

## Client usage

The command builder's cURL and Bench buttons send chat completions, which a decision model does not
serve. Ask questions on `/v1/systemone` instead:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "vllm-sr/d3",
  "state": "Write a Python function that merges two sorted lists.",
  "questions": {
    "kind": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What kind of work is this?",
             "criteria": {"code": "Writing or fixing code", "math": "Mathematics", "chat": "Anything else"}},
    "reasoning": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does answering this need multi-step reasoning?"}
  }
}'
```

Each answer carries the pick, the probability of every option, and `confidence`, the chosen option's
probability; a `noul` answer's value is the probability of yes. The probabilities are the checkpoint
runtime's (`model.system_one()`). Images and videos go in `images` and `videos` as http(s) or base64 data
URLs; vLLM places them before the text and reads them with the runtime's budgets (images up to 1.6
megapixels; videos at 2 fps, at most 32 frames):

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- <<EOF
{
  "model": "vllm-sr/d3",
  "state": "What does the attached image show?",
  "images": ["data:image/png;base64,$(base64 -w0 chart.png)"],
  "questions": {
    "kind": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What kind of image is this?",
             "criteria": {"chart": "A chart or plot", "photo": "A photograph", "document": "A document"}}
  }
}
EOF
```

A request takes up to 64 questions; a choice up to 255 options; a score 2 to 10 levels. A top-level
`instructions` field returns 400, since the prompt is fixed.

## Measured

On one AMD Instinct MI300X (ROCm 7.2), in a new Ubuntu 24.04 environment with empty caches and the ROCm nightly `0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`, against the checkpoint's own runtime (`AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)` with transformers 5.17.0 and flash-linear-attention 0.5.2) on 416 questions (text, JSON, a 40-option choice, an image and a video): 1 decision changed (a near-tie: the reference's two most likely answers were 0.002 apart); the median probability difference was 0.0025 and the largest 0.041. The same commands also gave the runtime's decisions on a text, an image and a video request.

On one AMD Instinct MI325X ([vllm-project/vllm#61565](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61565)), with the same mix of requests at 1, 8 and 64 concurrent clients, vLLM served 6.7, 8.6 and 8.5 requests per second, the checkpoint's own server (`d3_server.py`) 6.9, 6.1 and 4.6. vLLM's first answer came 215 s after `vllm serve` started with empty compile caches; `--max-model-len 32768` brings that to 139 s.

## Troubleshooting

- **`libmpi_cxx.so.40` or `libdw.so.1`: cannot open shared object file** when importing vLLM on ROCm: install
  `libopenmpi3t64` and `libdw1t64`.
- **Python version on ROCm**: the ROCm nightly wheels are built for Python 3.12 only (`cp312`); create the venv
  with `--python 3.12`, as above.
